claims.text: Machine-learning-based optimization of additive-manufacturing process conditions can overcome residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Machine-learning-based optimization can overcome degraded mechanical properties in AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
Machine-learning-based optimization can reduce the processing complexity associated with mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes.
The applicable laser-power range is 100–500 W.
The applicable scanning-speed range is 100–1000 mm/s.
The applicable powder-layer-thickness range is 20–50 μm.
The intervention applies to laser-based powder bed fusion.
The intervention applies to miniature components with a 10 mm × 10 mm × 10 mm build volume.
Grain structure is a structural mediator of the predicted mechanical-property improvement.
Porosity is a structural mediator of the predicted mechanical-property improvement.
Machine-learning-guided process optimization minimizes thermal gradients.
Minimizing thermal gradients reduces residual thermal stresses.
Optimizing grain structure improves mechanical properties.
Reducing porosity improves mechanical properties.
Machine learning simplifies processing by identifying optimal process windows.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 20% relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The intervention will increase ductility by 15% relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The intervention will reduce residual thermal stresses by 30% relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on the machine-learning algorithm, training-data quality, and component-geometry complexity.
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing yield strength, ductility, and residual stress between machine-learning-optimized and conventional high-thermal-load builds.
